decisions: Phase 5 is demand-driven and must not eagerly build a whole-compilation call graph.
BCL/LINQ known operations from Phase 4 keep precedence over source-method analysis.
Source calls must be resolved by IMethodSymbol and safe dispatch, not text-only names.
SourceMethodResolver classifies invocation targets as KnownOperation, SourceMethod, or Unsupported without analyzing callee bodies.
Source methods are considered available only through local DeclaringSyntaxReferences that resolve to MethodDeclarationSyntax.
Initial safe dispatch accepts static, private, ordinary nonvirtual, and proven sealed targets; virtual, interface, abstract, external, and unavailable-source calls remain Unsupported.
Cached method complexity is a template relative to the callee parameters, never a caller-bound expression.
Cycles are detected and return Unknown in Phase 5; recursion solving belongs to Phase 6.
Initial internal budgets are MaximumCallDepth = 5 and MaximumMethodsPerRootAnalysis = 32.
constraints: Do not modify inherited projects outside analyzer/.
Do not create ProjectReference, binary reference, local package dependency, or transitive dependency on inherited projects.
Do not add Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces, MathNet, or SymPy.

Do not implement recursion solving, recurrence extraction, Master Theorem, Akra-Bazzi, whole-solution call graph, external decompilation, full virtual hierarchy analysis, or CodeFixProvider in Phase 5.
Keep Unknown conservative for unresolved calls, unsafe dispatch, unavailable source, unproven argument binding, exceeded budget, and detected cycles.
Keep analyzer hot paths deterministic, cancellation-aware, concurrency-safe, and free from I/O, network access, process execution, and reflection-heavy behavior.
